tagline: The most electric-ready ferry market on the continent.
summary: Vancouver sits at the head of the Salish Sea with BC Ferries — one of the world's largest ferry operators, moving roughly 22.6 million passengers a year — actively electrifying through battery-electric Island Class vessels, and Harbour Air, which flew the world's first all-electric commercial seaplane in 2019. Together they make this a uniquely electric-ready ecosystem with dense commuter, tourism and cross-border demand across protected coastal water.

demand_signals.label: BC Ferries
demand_signals.note: One of the world's largest ferry operators; actively electrifying with battery-electric Island Class vessels + shore charging

demand_signals.label: Harbour Air
demand_signals.note: Flew the world's first all-electric commercial seaplane in Dec 2019 — premium demand and electric-readiness proof

demand_signals.label: Cross-border Salish Sea
demand_signals.note: Shared protected waters with Puget Sound

use_cases.title: Island & North Shore commuting
use_cases.body: Vancouver↔Victoria (~50 nm), ↔Nanaimo (~30 nm), and North Shore/Bowen (~8 nm) on silent zero-emission foils.

use_cases.title: Premium seaplane-class links
use_cases.body: City-to-city and Gulf-Island premium runs in a market already proven by electric seaplanes.

use_cases.title: Gulf Islands & cross-border
use_cases.body: Seasonal island-hopping and cross-border Salish Sea runs to the US San Juans.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Marquee crossings (Victoria ~50 nm, Nanaimo ~30 nm, North Shore/Bowen ~8 nm) sit inside the all-electric envelope over sheltered Salish Sea water; Harbour Air's electric seaplane proves the electric-ready demand.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Carries longer cross-border corridors (Vancouver↔San Juans ~65 nm) and Gulf-Island chaining with no charging dependency.

competitive_landscape: Today: BC Ferries (electrifying) and Harbour Air seaplanes. The pain is slow vehicle-ferry crossings and limited fast passenger options — the status quo a faster, cleaner foiling tier improves on.
seasonality: Year-round in sheltered waters; winter and open-strait crossings handled by routing and the hybrid.
regulatory_note: British Columbia has strong climate targets and a public mandate for BC Ferries to electrify with funded vessels and charging; Harbour Air's electric program signals deep regional support — an ideal regulatory environment.

precedents.what: A foiling-electric vessel network at national scale (~100 vessels / $100M, 3-year phasing)
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves foiling-electric works as an at-scale transfer-and-island-hopping network, not just a pilot.

sources.label: BC Ferries carries almost 23M passengers a year (one of the world's largest operators)
